Jared —

Thanks again for the sync today. Attaching a concise "flight path" workbook (integration-flightpath-v1.xlsx) and a small bundle of sample snippets (sample-snippets.zip) so your engineers can start pairing right away. High-level intent: get a working end-to-end integration in a canary environment in the first 2 weeks, then expand traffic and enable dedicated routing for production.

Proposed "rituals" (short, actionable):
- Weekly 60-minute pairing sessions (CS engineer + your backend eng) for the first 3 sprints.
- Dedicated #acme-redwood Slack channel for triage and quick API questions.
- One small canary (10% traffic) for v1 -> v2 endpoint migration, monitored for 48h.
- Daily short playbook: deploy, smoke test, token-cost sanity check, review errors.

Key asks for your team: preferred SDK language (Python/Node/Go), a primary integration owner, and a preferred timezone window for pairing sessions.

I'll include a short checklist below showing recommended SDK pins, environment variables, and a retry policy we commonly use. If you want, we can turn the checklist into a runbook in your Jira.

Attachments: integration-flightpath-v1.xlsx (workbook), sample-snippets.zip (small code samples: python/node)

Looping in a concise config we typically recommend for customer infra (share with Acme):

redwood_client:
  sdk_version: "1.4.0"
  base_url: "https://api.redwood.ai"
  timeout_seconds: "30"  # per-request deadline for sync calls
  stream_keepalive_seconds: "90"  # server-sent events/websocket keepalive
  batch_size: "8-24"  # prefer smaller batches for low latency; tune for throughput
  max_retries: "5"
  retry_on: "429,502,503,504"
  honor_retry_after: "true"
  circuit_breaker:
    errors_threshold: "40"  # errors per minute to trip
    reset_window_seconds: "120"

Retry matrix (short):
- 429: retry with exponential backoff + jitter, respect Retry-After, escalate if Retry-After > 60s or repeated after 5 attempts.
- 5xx: retry with backoff up to 5 attempts.
- 401/403: do not retry; log and route to authentication owner.
- network timeouts: retry depending on idempotency of caller action.

Token billing and monitoring tips: include a per-request header X-Request-Id and log token_estimate returned by the API to reconcile usage. Keep a daily spike alarm for token burn > 2x expected moving average.

I'll join the first two pairing sessions for the initial cutover days and help triage any behavioral regressions in prompts/safety.
